Both are detailed veto memoranda concerning claimed wartime-contract losses; both reject alleged assurances outside the written contractual arrangement, characterize payment as making the Government an insurer or underwriter of private losses, and warn of an undesirable precedent. C15 and C04 share the child's closing move of rejecting direct legislative payment while endorsing a judicial or jurisdictional remedy, but their overall factual and argumentative structures are less closely aligned.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"the contractor's claim is based primarily upon the premise that certain representations were made by Government officers at the time the contract was negotiated","parent_excerpt":"It is the Bank's representation that because the Ordnance Department knew of its furnishing these additional funds, it tacitly agreed to increase the price under the contract. So far as I can ascertain no responsible Ordnance Department officer or employee ... stated or implied that such was the case.","explanation":"Both reject attempts to impose additional Government liability based on alleged official assurances or implications beyond the formal wartime contract."},{"child_excerpt":"My approval of this bill would establish the undesirable principle of Government underwriting any wartime losses incurred by contractors","parent_excerpt":"the effect of which would be to make the United States an insurer of all the losses which the bank sustained on its loans to San Jose","explanation":"This is distinctive shared framing: special relief would improperly make the Government the underwriter or insurer of wartime commercial losses."},{"child_excerpt":"regardless of the fact that such contractors did not sustain a net loss","parent_excerpt":"the United States should bear all the risk arising out of such dealings while they should receive all the profits","explanation":"Both contrast the requested public assumption of losses with the claimant's retention of profits or other financial benefits."},{"child_excerpt":"I would, therefore, be willing to give my approval to a jurisdictional bill waiving the bar of any statute of limitations against the claim.","parent_excerpt":"I would, therefore, be willing to approve a bill which would permit a determination of the claimant's employment status ... notwithstanding any statute of limitations","explanation":"C15 provides a secondary close structural and verbal parallel for the child's alternative-remedy paragraph, though it is not the strongest overall template."}]}
